source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. The Diversity of India
points: India is enormously diverse in **languages, religions, food, dress, festivals, art** and **geography**.
Geography ranges from the **Himalayas** to coasts, deserts, plains and forests — shaping different ways of life.

sections.heading: 2. Threads of Unity — Sacred Geography
points: Beneath the diversity runs a deep **cultural unity**, expressed through a shared **sacred geography**.
**Pilgrimage (tirtha-yatra)** links distant places: the **Char Dham** — **Badrinath** (north), **Dwarka** (west), **Puri** (east), **Rameshwaram** (south) — connects the four corners of the land.
**Twelve Jyotirlingas** and other shrines are spread across India.
**Rivers** (Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Kaveri and others) are revered; the **Kumbh Mela** draws pilgrims from everywhere.

sections.heading: 3. Shared Stories and Traditions
points: The epics **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata** are known across the whole country in **many languages** and art forms.
Common **festivals, fairs (melas)**, music, dance and craft traditions cut across regions.
The idea of **Bharat** as one land — a cultural whole — is very old (see Ch. 2).

sections.heading: 4. "Unity in Diversity" / 'Many in the One'
points: India's genius is **"unity in diversity"** — many peoples, tongues and customs held together by shared values and sacred geography.
"**Many in the One**" captures this: countless local forms expressing one civilisation.
Diversity is a **strength**, not a weakness — the plural parts make a single, resilient whole.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Four language families: Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austroasiatic, Tibeto-Burman.
Char Dham: Badrinath (N), Dwarka (W), Puri (E), Rameshwaram (S).
12 Jyotirlingas; Kumbh Mela = great pilgrim gathering.
Ramayana & Mahabharata known across India in many languages.
Core idea = Unity in Diversity / 'Many in the One'.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Char Dham directions: Badrinath = **north**, Dwarka = **west**, Puri = **east**, Rameshwaram = **south** — match them correctly.
Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam belong to the **Dravidian** family (not Indo-Aryan).
"Unity in diversity" means diversity is preserved **within** a larger unity — not erased.
